title: Trees
summary: A **tree** stores **nodes** in parent-child relationships. Many tree problems repeat the same work on left and right children.
refresher: A binary tree **node** stores a **value** plus left and right child links. **Traversal** means visiting nodes in a chosen order. Most recursive tree **functions** start with a **null check**.
refresher_code:
if node is None: return base_answer
solve(node.left)
solve(node.right)

advanced-tree-root.title: Root is the starting node
advanced-tree-root.body: The **root** is the top **node** of the tree. **Traversal** usually begins there.
advanced-tree-root.example: root -> left child and right child
advanced-tree-root.notice: A missing **root** means the **tree** is empty.
advanced-tree-root.mistake: Do not confuse **root** with **leaf**. A root can have children.

advanced-tree-leaf.title: Leaf means no children
advanced-tree-leaf.body: A **leaf** **node** has no left or right child.
advanced-tree-leaf.example: node.left is null and node.right is null
advanced-tree-leaf.notice: **Leaves** are where many recursive paths stop.
advanced-tree-leaf.mistake: A **node** with one child is not a **leaf**.

sections.title: Tree node shape
sections.summary: A binary **tree** **node** has a value, left child, and right child.

blocks.body: A **tree** is made of **nodes**. In a **binary tree**, each node can have a left child and a right child. The first node is called the **root**.

blocks.title: Trace a tree traversal
blocks.caption: Visit the **node**, then the left side, then the right side.

steps.why: Preorder starts with the current **node**.

blocks.title: Tree words
items: Subtree: a smaller **tree** starting at some **node**.

blocks.title: Null checks come early
blocks.body: Most **tree** **functions** start by checking for `None`, `null`, or `nullptr`. Without that check, reading `node.left` on a missing **node** can crash.

choices: A node with exactly two children
blocks.why: A **leaf** is an end **node**. It has no left or right child.

sections.title: Read array-backed tree examples
sections.summary: Some practice prompts store tree levels in an **array** with placeholders for missing nodes.

blocks.body: A **level-order array** lists nodes from top to bottom and left to right. A placeholder such as `-1` means that position has no real node.

blocks.title: Turn a level array into a tree
blocks.caption: The array positions become parent and child slots.

steps.decision: Index 0 is the root.
steps.why: Index 0 is the root.

steps.title: Children of root

steps.decision: Indexes 1 and 2 are the left and right children.
steps.why: Indexes 1 and 2 are the left and right children.

steps.title: Missing child

steps.decision: `-1` means the left child slot is empty.

blocks.prompt: In a tree array, what does a placeholder such as `-1` usually mean?
choices: that position has no real node
blocks.why: The placeholder keeps the level positions aligned while marking an empty child slot.

blocks.body: **Traversal** means visiting every **node**. The three common depth-first orders use the same three actions: visit the node, traverse left, traverse right. Only the order of those actions changes.

blocks.title: Preorder: node, left, right
blocks.caption: Visit the current **node** before its children.

steps.title: Visit A first
steps.body: Preorder starts with the current **node**.
steps.what_changed: A is recorded before either subtree.
steps.decision: A is recorded before either subtree.
steps.why: Preorder starts with the current **node**.

steps.title: Go left to B
steps.body: After A, preorder moves into the left subtree.
steps.what_changed: B is recorded before B’s children.
steps.code_focus: trace trees: Go left to B
steps.decision: B is recorded before B’s children.
steps.why: After A, preorder moves into the left subtree.

steps.title: Visit D then E
steps.body: Preorder keeps using **node**, left, right inside the subtree.
steps.what_changed: D comes before E because D is B’s left child.
steps.code_focus: trace trees: Visit D then E
steps.decision: D comes before E because D is B’s left child.
steps.why: Preorder keeps using **node**, left, right inside the subtree.

steps.title: Finish right side
steps.body: After the left subtree is done, preorder visits C.
steps.what_changed: The final preorder is A, B, D, E, C.

state.note: order: A, B, D, E, C

steps.decision: The final preorder is A, B, D, E, C.

variables_after.name: state
variables_after.value: order: A, B, D, E, C

steps.why: After the left subtree is done, preorder visits C.

blocks.title: Inorder: left, node, right
blocks.caption: Finish the left side before recording the current **node**.

steps.title: Go left before A
steps.body: Inorder does not record A yet. It first walks left to B.
steps.what_changed: The current **node** waits until its left subtree is finished.
steps.code_focus: trace trees: Go left before A
steps.decision: The current **node** waits until its left subtree is finished.
steps.why: Inorder does not record A yet. It first walks left to B.

steps.title: Visit D
steps.body: D is the leftmost **node**, so D is recorded first.
steps.what_changed: Inorder often starts at the far-left **leaf**.
steps.decision: Inorder often starts at the far-left **leaf**.
steps.why: D is the leftmost **node**, so D is recorded first.

steps.title: Visit B then E
steps.body: After B’s left side, record B, then visit B’s right child E.
steps.what_changed: Inside each subtree, the pattern is still left, **node**, right.
steps.code_focus: trace trees: Visit B then E
steps.decision: Inside each subtree, the pattern is still left, **node**, right.
steps.why: After B’s left side, record B, then visit B’s right child E.

steps.title: Visit A then C
steps.body: Now A’s left subtree is done, so record A, then visit C.
steps.what_changed: The final inorder is D, B, E, A, C.

state.note: order: D, B, E, A, C

steps.code_focus: trace trees: Visit A then C
steps.decision: The final inorder is D, B, E, A, C.

variables_after.name: state
variables_after.value: order: D, B, E, A, C

steps.why: Now A’s left subtree is done, so record A, then visit C.

blocks.title: Postorder: left, right, node
blocks.caption: Finish children before recording the parent **node**.

steps.title: Go down first
steps.body: Postorder does not record A or B yet. It goes to children first.
steps.what_changed: Parents wait until their children are done.
steps.decision: Parents wait until their children are done.
steps.why: Postorder does not record A or B yet. It goes to children first.

steps.title: Record D then E
steps.body: D and E are **leaves**, so they can be recorded before B.
steps.what_changed: **Leaves** have no children waiting under them.
steps.code_focus: trace trees: Record D then E
steps.decision: **Leaves** have no children waiting under them.
steps.why: D and E are **leaves**, so they can be recorded before B.

steps.title: Record B
steps.body: B’s left and right children are done, so B can be recorded.
steps.what_changed: Postorder records the parent after both child paths **return**.
steps.decision: Postorder records the parent after both child paths **return**.
steps.why: B’s left and right children are done, so B can be recorded.

steps.title: Record C, then A
steps.body: C is done, then the **root** A is recorded last.
steps.what_changed: The final postorder is D, E, B, C, A.

state.note: order: D, E, B, C, A

steps.code_focus: trace trees: Record C, then A
steps.decision: The final postorder is D, E, B, C, A.

variables_after.name: state
variables_after.value: order: D, E, B, C, A

steps.why: C is done, then the **root** A is recorded last.

Visit left, then node, then right

sections.title: Return values from subtrees
sections.summary: Many **tree** **functions** combine left and right answers.

blocks.body: **Tree** **recursion** often asks the left child for an answer, asks the right child for an answer, then combines those two answers.

blocks.caption: Count **nodes** by counting left and right subtrees.

blocks.title: Read the return line
items: Adding them gives the full **tree** count.

blocks.prompt: A height **function** gets left height and right height. What should it **return**?
blocks.why: Height follows the longest path, so it uses the larger child height plus the current **node**.

sections.title: Level order uses a queue
sections.summary: Breadth-first **tree** **traversal** visits one level at a time.

blocks.body: Level-order traversal visits the **root**, then its children, then its grandchildren. A **queue** keeps that order because **nodes** that arrive first are processed first.

blocks.title: Level order uses queue order
blocks.caption: Use a **queue** to visit one **tree** level at a time.

steps.title: Start with root
steps.body: The **root** A is the first **node** waiting.
steps.what_changed: The **queue** starts with the top level.
steps.decision: The **queue** starts with the top level.
steps.why: The **root** A is the first **node** waiting.

steps.title: Visit A
steps.body: A **leaves** the **queue**, then B and C join.
steps.what_changed: The next level is waiting from left to right.
steps.decision: The next level is waiting from left to right.
steps.why: A **leaves** the **queue**, then B and C join.

steps.title: Visit B
steps.body: B **leaves** next because it waited before C. B adds D.
steps.what_changed: Children of B wait behind C, so level order is preserved.
steps.decision: Children of B wait behind C, so level order is preserved.
steps.why: B **leaves** next because it waited before C. B adds D.

steps.title: Visit C, then D
steps.body: C is processed before D because C was already waiting.
steps.what_changed: The final order is A, B, C, D.
steps.code_focus: trace trees: Visit C, then D
steps.decision: The final order is A, B, C, D.
steps.why: C is processed before D because C was already waiting.
